implementation_notes: Foundation supplies the primitives, not the pattern: encode the message, write it into the app's spool directory with Data.write(to:options:.atomic) (write to a temporary file plus rename), then call FileHandle.synchronizeFile() - which does not return until memory is flushed - and only then treat the send as accepted; remove the file after the peer acknowledged. An actor serializes spool state and replays the directory on launch, and a BGProcessingTaskRequest schedules retries when the app is not running. No iOS framework offers a durable queue for arbitrary messages, so the classic structure stays hand-written; where delivery is an HTTP upload, the OS-managed background session (next variant) replaces the spool.
pitfalls: An .atomic write is not a durability guarantee by itself - the bytes can still sit in the page cache, so synchronizeFile() is what makes the spool entry a commitment.
App suspension or termination kills in-flight sends, so replay must be driven from launch and from BGTaskScheduler, not from a background thread someone forgot.
The default data protection class makes the spool unreadable while the device is locked; set a class that allows background replay (for example completeUntilFirstUserAuthentication).
Container paths change between releases: persist message identifiers, never absolute file URLs, and clean the spool of entries whose ack was never received.

variants.name: OS-managed background URLSession upload
variants.implementation_notes: For HTTP sinks, Apple's background transfer system is the durable store and the retry engine: a URLSessionConfiguration.background(withIdentifier:) session hands upload tasks to the system daemon, which retries them across app suspension and termination and relaunches the app when a transfer completes (sessionSendsLaunchEvents = true; the app must call the stored completion handler in application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:)). Uploading from a file keeps the payload on disk until the transfer finishes. Use it where delivery is an HTTP request; anything that is not an upload/download (sockets, arbitrary protocols) needs the Foundation spool variant instead.
pitfalls: Background sessions only support upload and download tasks; a socket or custom protocol cannot be handed to the system this way.
The transfer is retried by the system, so the receiver sees duplicates: the request must carry an idempotency key and the server must dedup on it.
isDiscretionary = true lets the system delay delivery until convenient (charging, Wi-Fi) - a guarantee about eventual delivery, not about latency.
The file passed to uploadTask(fromFile:) must survive until the task completes; deleting it in the ack handler is safe, deleting it when the task is created is not.
